newsitem.title: USA: Mass. has rosy economic outlook for FY'98-experts.
newsitem.headline: Mass. has rosy economic outlook for FY'98-experts.

text.p: Economists told Massachusetts legislators that steady job creation, solid wage growth and low inflation would be the hallmarks Fiscal 1998.

But they warned that the projection call for only limited increases in spending because the economy in the Commonwealth was so good this year, even continued strong performance will mena only moderate hikes in tax revenues.
"The largest part of the growth process is behind us," Fredericak Breimyer, chief economist of State Street Bank, told the joint revenue-estimating session late Tuesday.

State Revenue Commissioner Mitchell Adams told the session, a meeting of the House and Senate Ways and Means Committees and the Office of Administration and Finance that he was anticipating state revenues of $12.667 billion for Fiscal 1998 that begins July 1.
State Street's Breimyer projected state revenues of $12.909 billion, while the Massachusetts Taxpayers Foundation, a good government group, projected $12.966 billion.
While the variation in the dollar amounts is due to slightly different calculation modesl, there was general agreement that the steep upward curve of recent economic performance was flattening out.
